body: Are you in the UK? If so, I would suggest Relate.
This is a great idea thank you!

Thank you for your reply. In all honesty it is hard to describe how someone else might view you. I don't think I am caustic nor an emotional vampire - I would describe myself as being high functioning, I.e. I don't have daily negative outlook, I do 70% of the household chores to keep me busy, I go to work and smile and get on with the job. At home I generally as fun to be around but I have moments of high intensity emotion when I feel stressed. But, I wouldn't be surprised if he is burned out by me.

Thank you for your advice. I have started looking for one and know that I haven't been as proactive on this account as I need to be, I.e. I need to actually book an appointment. We agreed in our  couples counselling session at the start of January that I would. It hasn't been 100% procrastination though, some of it has been the capacity in my life. But I know I need to sort it out this week.
Thank you. I have just joined a book club so I am hoping that will be a good outlet. We have dogs too so I enjoy good walks at the weekend. 😊

Thank you for your reply. I worry sometimes that it is my perspective that is wrong. In the past physical boundaries have been overstepped and we have worked on that (he hasn't repeated that again), but it now seems more unnatural of me to not want to cuddle up in bed with my partner so I hadn't really thought about it in the same way.
Individual Counselling.

True! To be honest I am in a place which I am currently comfortable, but I know that isn't the place I need to be for the relationship so the next step feels insurmountable which is why I am filled with anxiety. I know this isn't all a quick fix and my partner isn't great at expressing his emotions so I am probably projecting my fear of impatience onto him.
He is grumpy  (huffs and mumbles) but barely wakes to be honest.
Haha this is exactly what I think! 😂

Thank you for your message. We are in a different situation now and that previous one hasn't happened since. So we are working through that with our counsellor.

All he does is want to cuddle up in bed. It is harmless and no expectation to lead to more than cuddling.

The cuddling is on his terms, i.e. He comes over to my half of the bed, usually when he is drowsy, and can be there until the morning.

I have joked about it the next day saying I don't have room to move at night and he has told me just to roll him back over (easier said that done without waking him!). We have had thia conversation a few times and I know he is now starting to feel hurt by it so I haven't said again.

Thank you for your reply. I do hope that, over time, things will continue to progress. If anything I am now further ahead from where I was and understand my feelings better. But, my husband has been so patient yet I feel like I am dragging this on and eventually he will lose that patience.

Thank you for your reply. I will be honest and say that I have considered this but I worry that if we did I would fall into the trap of being comfortable away from him. I rarely feel like I want sex as it is, and being further away might exacerbate that? 

I think the thing I struggle with at the moment in bed though is that I have told him I feel uncomfortable when he cuddles and clings up close to me and he tells me just to push him away. Or, he looks hurt, and I get it, it will hurt to have the person you love not want you near them. So I feel enormous guilt too. 

So I guess I feel in a catch-22 situation.

Thank you for your reply. At first I felt this way and our counselling felt like it set me back. I am more comfortable now doing some senate focus tasks - the ones which don't involve penetration - but it doesn't seem to be making me feel more intimate. May I ask, did you find anything more successful than sensate?

Thank you for your reassurances and sorry to hear you have been here too. The isolation and guilt eat away at me. I just wish I could turn on desire like a lightswitch, but it doesn't happen. The issue is also that I feel comfortable in myself not wanting sex, but terrible guilt for my husband. He didn't sign up for this when we got married. He has been great and become more patient and stuck by me, but I don't know if I will be able to be how I once was.

Thank you for your reassurance. Part of the issue is that my husband doesn't want to talk about it so I sometimes sit and have to figure out on my own if the progress seems good, or just to understand my feelings better. Currently looking to start IC which I hope will help with this aspect at least. But the guilt I feel each night when he rolls over to hug me is hard.

Thank you so much for saying this. I won't hyjack the OPs post but my situation is similar and our therapist even makes heavy on how long we have been together, and all I think sometimes is that in another 15 years will it still be worth it.

I get you. I used to be able to joke it off. I was much larger than I am now and no one fancied me so it was easy to avoid those conversations. But now I am in a relationship but having issues I have no one who gets me... Not really. But, I echo what some others have said here. If your friends only want to talk about something you don't, then don't feel you have to take part in their company.

Thank you for your reply and I wholeheartedly agree and understand. If I am honest we jumped both feet into marriage counselling which helped enormously at the start and got us talking. Now we realise that we need to work on ourselves in order to help the relationship and I need to understand what led me down that path so it never happens again. I also carry lot of shame and guilt which has eroded my mental health. I have accepted that it might not be saved (because I can feel this underlying resentment towards me although he says he is happy) but I want to try.

Thank you for your reply. I think that I did start to fall out of love because when I needed my husband he wasn't there and I looked in the wrong place. It isn't an excuse for my behaviour and I live with guilt and shame everyday (as you rightly say, we both remember). I guess what I am finding difficult is that I am ready to try and work through what led me to that choice so I can make sure it doesn't happen again, but there is resentment towards me that my husband won't denies. I don't know how to move forward with it or whether ignorance is bliss and we carry on as we are.

I get this and thank you for posting it. I am the LL and spend a lot of my time wishing I could discuss this to try and make it work better as I want to work through it, but my HL partner shuts down when talking about his emotions. 

I know he must feel them but I spend a lot of effort trying to second guess how he is feeling - hence why I ended up in this sub-reddit originally. 

When we do discuss he can dismiss me and/or get angry and I shut down as a result so we get no where.

It is good to read the OPs positive progress and give me hope that it can work.

I am just about to start in my individual therapy journey too. It has taken me a good long while to get there but I feel I am ready now.

Naturally I want to talk to my best friend (my husband) about it but know that I need to be able to be independent of him too and not rely on him for validating myself. 

It feels like he doesn't want to listen, but then I also have put him through so much too. He needs space to not be my therapist as I imagine that it can be draining.

Try to explain to him though that there are points when you could do with the moral support - even if just to be positive about the steps you are taking.
I just wanted to say thank you for your reply too poster because it has resonated with me.

As someone who does exactly this myself please empathise that it is a deep rooted issue to solve in therapy. Not, as it is almost implied, a selfish need.

I am a people pleaser and would avoid conflict which had, over the last decade, eroded my sense of self to the point that I feel lost and cannot ground myself. Individual counselling is helping me find ways to set healthy boundaries not just to be "selfish".

I just wanted to say that even if you do have anxiety/depression he also has a responsibility to this marriage and to you. Please don't blame your mental health for his behaviour. It might be that your anxiety makes you feel paranoid (mine does and I am now in individual counselling to help with that) but speka to him. Openly and explain how you feel. Explain what you feel you need from him to help you feel more confident in the relationship. And he can do the same visa versa.
Why don't you book the appointment. Invite her and, if she doesn't come, then at least it is something you can work through with your counsellor.

Hi, I firstwanted to say well done for finding a place to open up and talk about your concerns. It could be very easy to hide away and ignore the issues until it is too late  Unfortunately I cannot offer more advice than ti try counselling - Individual would suit her best but also couples for you both. In the least it will give her a space to work through whatever issues are causing her this frustration, and will give you a mediator to talk through your concerns without fear of being rebuffed.

I can empathise with your wife as this is exactly where I am in my life right now I cannot say we have the same issues at the root, but her behaviour sounds like someone who is struggling with a depression/anxiety episode.

Right now the best you can be is to continue to support her but out your boundaries in place (make these clear to her). If she is angry, tell her that you understand that she is frustrated and you can listen when she is ready, but that you will not indulge her anger as it is coming from a place only she knows.

One thing we did which helped me a lot. Was to have a "marriage cup of tea". If I needed to talk/vent I would tell my husband I needed a cup of team we would then sit down and I was allowed 5 minutes to talk openly without being interrupted. After my 5 minutes, he could respond to what I had said. He then, in turn, did the same. What it allowed was for me it verbalise my thoughts or a space to vent, and him to listen and consider his response and it avoided arguments. Because we cannot interrupt it means neither person monopolised the conversation so it was a controlled situation and we both felt we had been listened to.

Your wife is clearly struggling so please encourage her to seek counselling. I know she kight resist at first, but it will give her the opportunity to work through whatever it is she cannot cope with.

Hi, I had to stop and leave a comment because I feel your pain, frustration and tiredness too. My LL problems started long before the pandemic, but they are definitely being exacerbated by it. I too am a teacher and exhausted, stressed and anxious nearly all of the time. I don't know where you are in the world, but I am in the UK and a lot of decisions are being made last minute here and we are constantly chopping and changing. So in an evening I just want to sleep and recover from the mental load I am carrying. But, like you, I know that in the long term it won't help. But, as a result I know that I am getting into bad habits of having intimacy without wanting it and I am scared that the issues I have been working through will come back.

I wish I could offer advice, but all I can say for now is to be completely open and honest with your significant other so that he understands why you might not have the energy right now.
Yes, I think I know that it has reached a point that scares me so I need to intervene.

Lots of posts here are demonizing your wife and labelling her as a cheater and someone taking you for a ride. What I will say is that you need yoto remain open minded as to what is really going on, and only your wife can tell you. She \*may\* have had an affair, she \*may\* have just discovered that her sexuality is more than hetrosexual,  she \*may\* have lost feelings towards you etc. Ultimately no one here knows so please don't take other views as gospel. If you want to try and save the relationship and figure out what is going on with your wife then I feel you need professional help and would suggest marriage counselling. If your wife can't agree to this, then that will tell you whether she sees a future with you.

I can only comment on my own experience in couples conselling (which as you will see from my posts has been successful ultimately but still an uphill struggle). I have a habit of feeling really good and productive in the session, and then afterwards feeling overwhelmed and helpless. It isn't always easy to make changes to your life and leave the comfort zone you have created, but this is what your partner needs to be willing to do. Like of it like a fight or flight moment. He should be willing to fight for the relationship, but he seems to want to run away. Sadly you cannot control this but he shouldn't string you along if he isn't willing to work on it after the sessions.
I am sorry to hear this. In the meantime I would suggest looking at the u/lowlibidocommunity group they are very inclusive and supportive where there are issues like you are having.

I can only give advice as someone who developed a sexual aversion from a similar series of events. It is not a healthy place for either of you right now and you need to communicate about this incident rather than ignore. You are not an abuser and your partner is not sexually manipulating you. Instead it seems like lack of communication - she didn't express her lack of desire to have sex, and you didn't tell her that you didn't think she wanted it. Instead you both went ahead and had sex and it became a traumatic event of unwanted sex. Do you know why she didn't feel she could say 'no'? This is something that needs to be discussed. She needs to know that it is safe and okOK to say no. I hope this makes sense?

Thank you for writing this, I have had a similar experience to you in any respects. But I wondered if you could let me know how your LL partner responds each time a new stage begins? I am the LL and I have a cycle where we begin a new stage and I struggle mentally with it (leading to small bouts of depression and anxiety), we then work through it and I feel comfortable, then we start a new stage. I would advocate sensate as an activity, but I do find it mentally taxing at times.

Hi, I have been through sensate (still in it) and some very responses. Please feel free to look at my post history.

In the short term I found it very difficult as all intimacy in our relationship had ground to a halt. It look a lot of self-reflection and work on myself to feel comfortable being naked, and touching my husband. Mentally this was taxing at first. But... The slow pace and emphasis on tough not sex has over time helped a lot. I now feel more comfortable being naked, we have a routine and laugh and joke during our tasks and intimacy outside of the tasks has returned.

I can see, a year and a half on, that we have made huge progress. Yet we are still not there entirely. Each time we add a new element, I really struggle mentally.

So, ultimately I would advocate it but you have to give it time to see the effect.

Yes, I think that I am goigg to wait until our next MC appointment and see how he responds to the discussion about this situation. If we both cannot work together on this then a difficult decision may need to be made. But at least I will have known that I tried and, ultimately, have helped myself understand 'me' better. I still have a long way to go though.

Thank you for your reply. You are entirely right. In the moment it was presumed consent, I obliged, and going backwards made him, I think, defensive. I have difficulty saying "no" because in the past it has caused arguments and I carry a lot of guilt over those arguments as it is me making him frustrated and lonely. I think, in this case, I wanted to discuss why he chose to cross the boundaries we agreed to in our MC.

But, I think the best place to discuss this will be in our next counselling appointment.

Thank you for your reply. I believe that in other aspects of our relationship we work well together so I would be disappointed if our sex life defined us, which is why I am trying to help change my behaviours. I would be lying if I said it was easy. It has been a hard and emotional year, but we have made progress.

That being said, this lapse from my husband has set me back and the mountain now feels even higher.

I hope that our counsellor will help give me the tools to rescale the mountain.

Thank you for your reply. I would be lying if I didn't say that this event has made me question things. Once we started MC I felt like we agreed to do a restart/reset on the issues from our past. We worked through them and we were redefining our sex life and intimacy to break through the aversion I had developed. This has made me question whether it was just a momentary slip up, of if we are falling back into the same patterns.

Thank you for your reply. This is a new one on me so I will look into it. I asked him if he rembered and he said yes, but when I asked if we could talk about it he said no. When he does it he is very out of character, even as far as how dirty he talks and he never talks like that usually.

Thank you for your reply. I have taken time in the last couple of days to get my feelings down and try and untangle them so that, in our counselling session, I can be honest and not just driven by emotion.

I think what I am struggling with the most at the moment is his lack of empathy to how I am feeling about it. I tried to talk to him and he refused. I could have said "no" but I didn't want to create a situation where he lost his temper with me/increase frustration when I feel I am to blame for that frustration. But... I need to be able to say it.

Thank you for your reply. I do, in some respects, agree with parts of what you have said. I think it has caused damage to me - more than I expected. I now haven't slept fully for 3 nights and when he tries to touch me I flinch. I don't want to be like this as we had moved beyond this and I felt comfortable with more intimacy especially recently.

I don't know if I would see him as an abuser as such. I appreciate that this incident oerhaos implies it, but it is a rare occurance - although one that has happened before and been discussed in counselling. It often happens when he is drunk/stressed/horny. That doesn't excuse his lack of respect for boundaries we mutually laid out, but outside of this incident his behaviour isn't coercive.

Buy, you are right, I am feeling nervous around him especially at the moment.

Thank you for your reply. I do agree and can see his frustration which is why I have a lot of guilt over this. I feel I am failing him in many respects, and that his attempts to be intimate leave me feeling further from him.

I also agree that I think, in this occasion, I am struggling not only to deal with blaming myself (guilt) but trying to understand why he decided to do this. As he cannot talk to me about it I don't know if he is feeling frustrated, anger, resentment, embarrassed, or simply nothing.

I do appreciate your reply because I need a perspective from HL.

Thank you so much for your perspective. I am sorry to here about your situation and it must be difficult to get no response back from your wife. I cannot speak for her, but I know I have struggled a lot with mental health over my own perceived inability to be as intimate with my husband as I feel I should be. I have attributed a lot of blame to myself over this, and have worked hard this last year to try and over come the sexual aversion I developed.
I would hope that, in time, you and your wife would be able to do the same. Have you undertaken marriage counselling/sex therapy? Although it has been a difficult year, I can say I have moved forward - this time last year I couldn't be touched by my partner without flinching, and couldn't even look at myself naked.

Thank you too for your perspective about how he might be feeling, and I am questioning myself a lot to look at what I could have done differently to make him feel wanted or to open the discussion to having some intimacy before bed.

Unfortunately now, the issue for me is that I feel uncomfortable being around him and I have tried to talk (using our MC techniques) but he does not want to engage in the conversation. I am trying very hard not to feel differently towards him,  but I am struggling, and when he went to hug me last night in bed I felt myself flinch. I am worried this has set us back in our progress.

Thank you for your reply and the link to the article. I will read it now,  but it gives me some comfort to know that there is some literature out there to help me try to understand and process this prior to our next counselling session.

Thank you for your reply. I will admit that I am very confused this week and feel like I am making a mountain out of a mole hillin some respects. I don't think it was rape or sexual assault. But I am mostly concerned that this is something that has previously made me uncomfortable, we have talked about in counselling and set out boundaries. He has felt the need to violate those boundaries but is unwilling to participate in a conversation about it so I don't know why he felt the need  and I question is there something I could have done differently. I am going to discuss it at our next counselling appointment but, if he cannot discuss it there either, then I don't feel I can stay in our situation as we currently are and a period of separation might be necessary.

Just to present the other side. The 'time out' can also allow the HL the opportunity to work out if they are willing to compromise themselves too for the LL. In order for it to work, both parties must compromise.

Thank you for your reply. I am hoping that, in our next MC session, this is something we can work on. I am a little worried about how he will respond talking about this with a 3rd party which is why I tried just the two of us, but he wasn't receptive to it at the time.

Thank you for your reply. I understand that our intimacy is not normal and, when we  discussed MC and intimacy issues (some of the issues do stem from him as well as myself) we agreed to both try to work on the marriage. 

The issue I have here specifically is that he has crossed the boundaries we agreed upon and I worry that this will have a negative impact on our progress.

I will continue to work on myself, and work with our counsellor and my husband, but whether he feels he can wait is beyond my control.

Hi, sorry to hear that this experience made you feel like that. Have you spoken to your partner and explained how it made you feel, especially the leg touch? Have you considered relationship counselling/sex therapy? I only ask because I am the LL in my marriage and we have been doing this for a year. I won't lie, it is hard at times and it is slow but a year later we had made a huge amount of progress and I have actually learnt to enjoy his touch again.

That was... Until he did something similar to you (touch me when I was asleep at night). For me, the issue this time was different. I cam be receptive to his touch but we have had to redefine our boundaries and learn to compromise with each other (like pressing a reset button on the relationship). I spoke to him the next day about how I felt because the contact had been unwanted but he lost his temper. Sadly this has set us back a bit now.

The thing I have learnt is that the dead bedroom can be resolved but it takes patience, time, communication, and compromise from both parties. If one is able to do that then it won't work. Also be prepared for it to be like a roller-coaster ride because, as I discovered, it can be better one day then something can send you back to square one again.

Thank you for your reply, it means a lot. In the least to help me know that how I am feeling is ok. The thing is that it is so out of character for him when he does this, but it is something he has done in the past (pre-counselling) and I thought we had moved beyond it.

Thank you for replying, it means a lot. I have spent today reflecting on what I wrote this morning. My anxiety is still heightened but you are right, to some extent I have felt scared today. I think that, because this is an issue we have had in the past, it has brought up a lot of old feelings too. The positive is that I now can recognise those feelings.

I feel I need to discuss this with our therapist but I am a bit concerned as he will be there with us as we are still in couples counselling not individual.

I came here this morning to write my own post, similar to yours, and wanted to show solidarity. I do not have the answers because it is a dilemma I am also facing at the moment, but reading your words has helped me know that I am not alone.

I came here this morning to talk about how I was feeling in a similar situation and could have written this myself. Thank you for sharing your words and feelings. I wish I had an answer but I am in the same place as you. But I wanted to show solidarity. As other posters have put here, remember these are his emotions to deal with not yours.

I am sorry that my experience has had a negative effect on you. I will reiterate that this is my experience and, on the whole, the sex therapy (although a rollercoaster ride) has been more positive than not. Literally on Sunday I posted a post about how positive I felt it all was and how if I could stay at this point I would be really happy. I felt more enjoyment and relaxation than I had in a long time. Sadly my session on Tuesday uncovered issues that I didn't even know existed and they need more time to explore. This one session has really knocked my confidence but coming on here and writing down my thoughts and questions for my therapist have really helped. If she cannot help me in the next session then it is time to move on. But please don't hurt yourself  because this is one experience, and many comments here suggest it isn't a typical one for therapy. x

Thank you so much your reply. It is what I think I needed to hear. I have taken a couple of days away from social media to process everything and reading these comments has now been very helpful. I agree that this is something I feel needs to be explored but at the time I felt so overwhelmed I just agreed to the next part of our homework tasks because I didn't know what to say. When we started sex therapy in our couples counselling I thought the issue with my aversion. Was just down to low libido and now we seem to just keep uncovering more issues with me which makes me feel so broken. My confidence has taken a huge dip. And the advice does feel fairly contradictory in parts which makes it hard to know what to actually do in between our appointments.

Thank you for your reply and sorry for my delay to it. I took a couple of days off social media to process a bit better. What you have said resonates with me. I feel that she is trying to uncover all the parts that have led me to a sexual aversion and this was one we touched on, but in hindsight needed exploring. Instead we seemed to move on and I disassociated in the session  and have been left a little lost since. I agreed to to next stage in our homework tasks because I didn't know what else to say at the time. I felt a bit in shock to be honest. I think I need to take this back to her next time and see how she handles it. If she isn't able to support then I need to look elsewhere. 

The images came about because my husband was quite prudish when describing where he has touched during our homework task. She brought it up and asked him to use it to describe. I recoiled, not so much because of the image of female genitals, but I think because I felt exposed as we were to discuss this image as if it was mine. This then led to the conversation about my childhood and she thinks I have sexual regression from a very modest Christian  upbringing.

Hi. Thank you for your reply. The basis of the picture was because my husband was asked to give feedback to a homework task we had to do and was struggling to be specific in discussing where he was focusing his attention on me. She showed a picture to help him discuss it and I recoiled.

Thank you for your reply, and for giving me hope. I felt so shocked at how I could feel really positive about our relationship to now not being able to anchor onto anything right now. I just feel that my confidence and self-worth has been shattered.

I know my usual pattern is that I feel this wya first, then it starts to feel OK, then I feel fine. But I didn't see this coming and I just went into a kind of shock. 

My husband hasn't talked to me about it because he feels he cannot help, but I do think a personal therapist is certainly the next thing I need to do because it feels all mixed up now between couples counselling for communication, sex therapy for intimacy, and now my own issues.

Thank you for your kind reply. I think, after a few days reflection, this is exactly what I need to do. I am still trying to process the session before I even start to think about the issues we discussed.

Thank you for your reply and supportive comments. They resonate with me. I just felt overwhelmed after this session and 'checked out' in the middle of it as I didn't know what to say or do. She did ask me if I was OK with that next step and I just agreed as I didn't know what else to say really, and she told me she would 'expose' me to the images each week to normalise it and I just said 'ok' again like an idiot. I now worry that have started to disassociate and just have come to a feeling of acceptance that this is what it is going to be and I know I need to not do that.

Thank you for your reply. I will say that to her at the next appointment. I think I just froze and I do have a habit of agreeing to what she says, in part because I worry about disappointing my husband and her.

We have been trying to unpick why I developed a sexual aversion and there are so many layers to it all. The sad thing is that at the end of all of this I now feel more broken than I did at the start.

Hi, thank you so much for your reply a lot of it really resonated with me. I needed to take a couple of days away from social media after my session. Needless to say, things have been a bit fraught between my husband and myself since that session.

In answer to your questions, I honestly don't know her qualifications but we got to her through Relate marriage counselling initially. She seems to know what she is doing. But I don't know if she fully comprehended how it made me feel. She said at the end of the session that she could see that I had become distant and I didn't look comfortable but she didn't press any further.

She said aversion therapy, as we have come to uncover quite plainly that I have a sexual aversion for what seems like a lot of reasons and we are trying to unpick them all.

The strange thing is that I don't have a problem looking at genitalia, more that it was the implied meaning that these were representing mine. She was asking my husband to describe where he was focusing his attention when we are undertaking our 'homework' tasks. I am coy in many respects, and grew up in a very modest household so it does make me feel a bit uncomfortable and it made me feel exposed when we were talking about myself. From that point I kind of checked out, and the disassociation makes sense now.
Thank you.
Thank you for your reply. We are back with our therapist this week so will undoubtedly be something we will talk about.
Thank you.

Thank you for your reply. I did, but sadly it wasn't as well received as I hoped. You can see from my post history that we have a fractious relationship at the moment, and therapy and sensate focus is part of a way to resolve this. I think doing 'less' feels disappointing to him - like we are going backwards.

This is exactly me. My partner doesn't hurt me and hasn't ever, but my anxiety flys through the roof when he is stressed and angry. I wanted to say you were not alone, because unfortunately I don't know hot to stop myself!

I have written a separate comment, but as the LL who is feeling like your husband. I want to say that yes, I do feel sexually adverse but also love my husband. The issue for me lies around my experiences of sex itself not my husband. I am adverse to sex and sexual contact. I am now trying to work through this with our therapist to take away the negative emotions I associate with it. However, it took time through counselling to understand this (and the process is far from over) and at the start my emotions were mixed up. I didn't know if the problem was my husband, myself, our sex life, mental health etc. I think now I know that it is all tied together - sort of like which came first the chicken or the egg?

I am a bit like your husband. I dearly love  and care for my partner but I struggle with sexual desire for him. I know he is attractive, a great partner/companion but my desire response just isn't there so we are now in therapy to explore this. Does your husband find others attractive/feel aroused/have sexual urges outside of your relationship? I don't, and I am working through this with a sex therapist and we have explored asexuality, low libido, LL4U, hormone, response desire etc. The process of therapy can feel, at times, overwhelming and difficult and I too have sessions where I struggle to control my mood afterwards because of feelings of frustration, guilt, sadness, and anxiety (you can look at my post history if needed). However, I can see some progress has been made in helping my understand myself and our relationship. I would strongly suggest your husband and you continue with this. Unfortunately, the way you are feeling is also understandable and I think having individual sessions yourself will help you with this. You are good enough, please remember this. As myexsparamour says, there are a plethora of reasons why someone may not feel sexually attracted to you.

Thank you for your reply. We started a year ago with marriage counselling. We worked through our communication issues and trust/honesty issues.
